To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HIV-protease saquinavir is effective against cervical cancer cell lines in vitro and that this effect does not involve the proteasome.
HIV-protease-inhibitor saquinavir is effective against cervical cancer in vitro and that its mechanism of action is independent from proteasome inhibition.
the HIV-protease-inhibitor saquinavir reduces cell proliferation, invasion and cell survival in cervical cancer cell models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of innovative therapies in CC and the identification of new molecular targets.
the development of innovative therapeutic strategies against CC, and the present results demonstrate for the first time that saquinavir can be considered a promising agent for this purpose.
the use of HIV-protease-inhibitors as a new class of anticancer drugs, and in particular with the use of saquinavir as a promising therapeutic agent for CC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
saquinavir, in a proteasomal independent manner, is able to reduce cell proliferation, invasion and cell survival in cervical cancer cell line models.
HIV-PIs are able to exert antineoplastic activities in CC cell lines.

the use of saquinavir, as a single agent or as an adjuvant to other therapeutic agents, could represent a novel and promising approach in the treatment of CC, especially in patients with advanced or relapsed disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
saquinavir, a drug used in HIV treatment, is able to exert direct antitumour activities in preclinical models of cervical cancer.
the HIV-protease-inhibitor saquinavir reduces cell proliferation, cell migration and cell clonogenicity of CC cell lines in vitro, in a proteasomal activity-independent manner.
the HIV-protease saquinavir is an antineoplastic compound that could be used in the treatment of CC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV-protease-inhibitors can have antineoplastic activity in cervical cancer cell line models.
saquinavir, a proteasome inhibitor used in HIV therapy, is able to reduce cell proliferation, invasion and colony formation in a proteasomal-independent manner in in vitro models of CC.

saquinavir, an HIV-protease-inhibitor, is able to significantly inhibit cell proliferation, clonogenic potential and cell invasion, but not cell radiosensitivity, of human cervical cancer cell lines in a proteasomal activity-independent manner.
